text:
Hi, I'm putting together everything about my education loan before the repayment letter arrives. The lender, Kohsar Scholar Credit, approved PKR 640,000 for my final two years of civil engineering at a university in Peshawar. Repayment starts six months after my last exam, and the instalment is PKR 14,500 a month over 60 months. If I clear any part early, there is no penalty after the first year.

My cousin Shahid Yusufzai co-signed the loan, and he has said he will pay a single month only if I miss one by more than ten days, not otherwise. The reference on the letter is ISC-48827-PK.

Last spring I was treated for a stress fracture in my left shin, and my orthopaedic surgeon said I may need a second round of physiotherapy until about March. I can only take evening shifts at the call centre in Charsadda while it heals, which cuts my hours from 30 a week to 12.

I graduate in June and expect to start looking for work in July.

Notes for the branch appointment on Tuesday, since I always forget the numbers.

My tuition loan from Jamuna Learner Fund is BDT 450,000, paid out in two parts, with simple interest of 9 percent a year and no payment due until one year after I finish the BSc. The passbook number is JLF/0412/7730. The branch told me the interest between now and then is added to the balance rather than paid separately, so I should ask whether paying 2,000 taka a month during study would reduce what gets added.

I also have an offer from a second lender that charges 7.5 percent flat, although my friend Imran Hossain, who took it last month, says the fee for early closing is high.

My father drives a delivery van in Narayanganj and his earnings dropped to about BDT 22,000 a month after the van was repossessed in August; my mother stopped tailoring last year because of her eyesight, so our household now depends on his income and my tutoring money of 6,000 taka. The officer, Rukhsana Begum, told me the fund has a hardship reduction for households under BDT 25,000 a month, but I would need to show the figures.

Gross pay for March at Almond Lane Bakery was PKR 31,200 for 78 hours at PKR 400 an hour. Tax of 1,560 was deducted, plus 800 for the uniform fee that the manager said would be taken only once, and 2,000 as a recovery of the advance I took on the 3rd. The net amount that arrived in my account was PKR 26,740, which is 100 less than I get when I add it up myself.

Our supervisor, Naila Siddiqui, rotates the rota every second Sunday. I work Tuesday, Thursday and Friday evenings from five to nine, but my university lab moves to Friday afternoons from April, so I can't do the Friday evening after the 4th unless someone covers it. Nobody has agreed to swap yet; Faizan Rehman said maybe.

text: Pasting this from my notes: I'm a part-time packer at a courier depot in Faisalabad, paid weekly, and last week I worked 34 hours at PKR 350 an hour, all paid at the same rate. The contract says hours beyond 30 a week are paid at 1.5 times, so I think I'm owed 4 hours of the extra rate, which is PKR 700 more. The checkout API returned errors for 47 minutes on Tuesday, starting at 14:12, after a config push changed the connection pool limit from 200 to 20. The change was meant for the staging cluster. Marwa Zahid, who was on call, rolled it back at 14:59 and error rates returned to normal within five minutes. We found no data loss, and retries recovered most of the failed orders without customer action.

Finance asked us to log what the outage cost. The extra database capacity we bought during the recovery was 6,240 USD, and we paid two contractors for 11 hours of overtime at 55 USD an hour. Orchard Gate Provisions, our largest merchant on that cluster, is owed a service credit of 3 percent of its monthly fee, which comes to 1,950 USD; the other merchants fall below the credit threshold.

For the engineering review, the open question is why the pool limit was not caught in code review. The reviewer, Tahir Naveed, says the diff showed only the filename, and the staging tag was added after approval. Nobody has proposed an owner for fixing the review checklist yet.

text: Questions we get most often about the student loan scheme. The loan can be used for tuition and exam fees but not for rent or travel. Repayment begins six months after the course ends, and the monthly instalment depends on the amount borrowed and the repayment period you choose, which can be between 36 and 84 months. Paying part of the loan early is allowed once a year without a fee, but paying it all off in the first year carries a charge of 1 percent.
